447: Built around Chosen, Cultist Mobs, Defilers, Huron Blackheart, Abaddon the Despoiler, Masters of the Maelstrom, and Chaos Terminators, this list pairs the Cabal of Chaos detachment's Dark Pact buff — granting psyker ranged attacks +1 Strength — with the Fellhammer Siege-Host's incoming-wound subtraction to create a gunline that hits harder than it looks and absorbs punishment better than it should. The plan is to flood midfield with Cultist screens and Chosen while Defilers and Dark-Pact-fuelled psykers grind out kill points, letting Abaddon and Terminators seal contested objectives once the enemy screens are stripped. It punishes elite low-volume armies that rely on Strength-overkill shooting to remove tough targets, since Fellhammer's wound-roll penalty blunts exactly that trade. Horde-flooding and high-AP melee that bypasses the Siege-Host's defensive trigger will crack the force open.
448:
Built around Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Warpsmith support, Cultist Mob screens, and Vashtorr the Arkifane, this list runs the Cabal of Chaos detachment with most lists also taking Soulforged Warpack — stacking Dark Pact synergies across Daemon Vehicles to turn already-threatening chassis into overloaded anti-armour platforms that punch up in both shooting and melee.

The win condition is grinding through enemy armour and heavy infantry by activating Soulforged Warpack's wound-roll bonus on Venomcrawlers and Defilers simultaneously, while Cultist Mobs hold objectives cheaply and Vashtorr amplifies the Daemon Vehicle core through his native support tools.

It punishes elite-heavy and vehicle-dense lists that can't clear multiple big-bodied threats at once, forcing opponents into impossible threat-priority decisions across several hard targets.

Massed low-AP chip damage and cheap screen-flooding crack it open — if the Cultist screens die early and the Dark Pact Leadership tests are exploited, the expensive Daemon Vehicle core is left exposed and unable to reliably activate its contracted bonuses.
450: Built around Wyches, Incubi, Lady Malys, Lelith Hesperax, and Drazhar packed into a fleet of Raiders and Venoms, this list is a layered skimmer assault force running both Exhibition Of Slaughter and Skysplinter Assault — every disembark grants Lance on melee weapons and Ignores Cover on ranged, while Wych Cult melee attacks gain Lethal Hits against non-vehicles. The win condition is stacking those disembark bonuses to delete priority targets in one coordinated wave, then flooding objectives with horde bodies before the opponent can recover. It punishes infantry-heavy lists brutally — Lethal Hits into Lance-boosted melee with mass Wych bodies creates anti-horde overload that soft targets simply cannot survive. The weakness is durability: the transports are the engine, and any list packing anti-tank overload or volume heavy fire can ground the skimmers and strand lethal units before they ever get to swing.
466: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Defilers, Tormentors, Lord Exultants, winged Daemon Princes, Lucius the Eternal, and Chaos Rhinos in the Coterie of the Conceited detachment, this is a transport-heavy assault force that bets on controlled aggression. The engine is the Pact points pledge system — you declare how many units you'll kill each round, deliver on that number, and bank the reward, making precise threat sequencing more important than raw volume. It punishes mid-range infantry-heavy lists through mobile anti-armour from Defilers and mechanised Flawless Blades pressuring multiple lanes simultaneously. The crack is consistency: the pledge mechanic punishes over-commitment hard, and a resilient, low-unit-count opponent makes hitting your pledge target nearly impossible.
473: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, Grand Master Voldus, Brotherhood Chaplains, and supporting Strike and Interceptor Squads, this list runs the Argent Assault detachment to ensure Paladins wound up even when punching into high-Toughness targets. The win condition is layered melee pressure across multiple fronts — Paladins grind through elite infantry and monsters while Terminators, frequently supplemented by Hallowed Conclave's Fell Back and fight/shoot ability, contest and reclaim objectives without surrendering board presence after a bad combat. It punishes slow, durable armies that rely on Toughness to survive melee, since the core detachment strips that defensive buffer from Paladins entirely, and the mobile toolkit of Interceptors keeps the pressure spread wide. However, high-volume shooting lists that can strip Paladins before they engage, or armies that deny the melee phase through layered screens, crack this build open by neutering the wound-roll engine before it fires.
481: Built around the Knight Castellan as its undeniable centerpiece, this list uses the Dominus Foebreakers detachment to grant Dominus-class Knights +1 to hit against units sheltering in terrain, punishing the common tournament habit of hiding key pieces inside ruins. The plan is to leverage that accuracy bonus on the Castellan's massed firepower to delete dug-in threats early, then use a flexible supporting roster — Destriers, Warglaives, and Helverins cycling in as needed — to control board space and grind scoring turns. It excels against armoured or elite armies that rely on terrain cover for safety, since the detachment ability strips away that defensive calculation entirely. Where it struggles is against fast, aggressive forces that can close the gap and tie up the Castellan in melee before it fires, or lists that flood cheap bodies to deny objectives the big Knights can't efficiently contest.
480: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Armiger Helverins, a Knight Crusader, and a Knight Castellan, this list floods the table with medium and large walkers across every threat range. The plan is to apply relentless anti-armour pressure from multiple angles simultaneously — Helverins suppress at range while Warglaives chase down vehicles and monsters in melee, forcing opponents to split resources and concede priority targets. It punishes armour-heavy lists badly, stacking mobile anti-armour output that most vehicle-dense builds simply cannot absorb across multiple turns. Where it struggles is against elite infantry and screens: the list lacks the concentrated anti-horde volume to efficiently clear bodies off objectives, leaving it vulnerable to anything that can park cheap wounds in the way and deny scoring.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard packed into Kapricus Carriers and Hekaton Land Fortresses, supported by Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Kâhl, Hernkyn Pioneers swarming objectives, and Hernkyn Yaegirs threatening flanks, this is a brawling gunline that closes distance aggressively and fights at close range. The Hearthguard Covenant's re-roll wound rolls of 1 within 9" rewards getting elite infantry into short range, turning every close-quarters shooting phase into a punishment rack, while YP generation from unit destruction fuels additional ability cycling. It excels against elite low-model-count armies where its mass of high-quality short-range firepower and resilient infantry can isolate and delete targets one at a time without bleeding out. However, aggressive skew lists that force attrition across a wide front strain its relatively low unit count, and opponents who deny the 9" engagement bubble strip the core wound-reroll engine entirely.
482: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Knight Castellans, Cerastus Knight Lancers, Knight Crusaders, and Armiger Helverins under the Freeblade Company detachment, this list fields a full court of Knights that each carry Feel No Pain 6+ and tick back a wound every Command phase, making every model a war of attrition rather than a glass hammer. The plan is to push mobile anti-armour pressure across the entire table — Lancers and Warglaives threatening flanks and vehicles while Castellans and Crusaders saturate midfield with layered firepower — grinding opponents down through sustained damage and a durability curve that makes trades consistently favor the Knights side. It punishes lists built on spiking single large threats off the table in one turn, because the wound-regen and FNP keep every Knight relevant longer than the math suggests. It cracks against mass mortal wounds or volume high-AP shooting that overwhelms the regen before it can matter.
456: Built around Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, Canoptek Doomstalkers, and the Void Dragon, this Canoptek Court list plays a relentless mid-board control game anchored on the Power Matrix — projecting dominance from your deployment zone outward by contesting No Man's Land objectives to extend buffs across the battlefield. The engine is resilience and board saturation: Technomancers keep Wraiths and Doomstalkers cycling back into the fight while Doomstalkers punish anything that tries to clear your objective presence, with Dimensional Sanctum (in over half of lists) letting key characters ghost out of danger. It punishes slower, attrition-averse armies that can't clear durable, reanimating bodies turn after turn. However, high-volume anti-infantry or elite combat threats that can delete Wraith squads before Reanimators act will crack the regeneration loop and collapse the entire board-hold plan.
486: Built around near-five squads of Boyz backed by Painboyz, Warbosses, Bigbosses, Ghazghkull Thraka, and Wazdakka Gutsmek, all operating under the Green Tide detachment that grants Boyz units of 10+ models a 5+ invulnerable save. The plan is to flood the midboard with durable, save-stacked infantry blobs, using Painboyz to sustain them through attrition while Ghazghkull and Warbosses drive kill efficiency — scoring through sheer presence and melee dominance rather than finesse. It punishes low-volume shooting armies hardest, since the 5+ invulnerable save forces opponents to commit enormous resources to strip blobs that simply refuse to evaporate. Massed high-quality firepower — especially mortal wound output or anti-horde weapons that bypass the invulnerable save at scale — can delete blobs faster than Painboyz can patch them, cracking the list before it smashes home.
487: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, Beastboss, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Mozrog Skragbad, Kill Rigs, and a gretchin screen, this is Da Big Hunt in full expression — a wall of Beast Snagga bodies backed by elite squig cavalry crashing into midboard every game. The engine is Da Big Hunt's Prey designation: lock onto an enemy monster, vehicle, or character, then funnel charge re-rolls into Squighog Boyz and Beastbosses to guarantee contact and rip the target apart, cascading kills into secondary scoring while Kill Rigs anchor and bully the midfield. It punishes elite low-model armies viciously — anti-tank overload from multiple squig hammer units overwhelms anything that relies on one or two key vehicles or monsters to hold the line. Spread damage and volume fire crack it open, since the build folds when its charge threats are whittled through attrition before they can make contact.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, two-plus Infernus Squads, Land Raider Redeemers, and Librarians operating under Forgefather's Seekers, this list floods the board with melta and flame infantry delivered in armoured transports, supported by Bladeguard Veterans and Adrax Agatone holding flanks. The engine is the Seekers' Companions synergy: Infernus Squads become eligible to advance-and-shoot via Vulkan's presence, and the Assault keyword on all ranged weapons lets the whole force push up aggressively while the +1 Strength inside 12" turns flamer and melta profiles into armour-cracking tools, with Librarians cycling Divination or Pyromancy each round to stack re-rolls or extra punch onto priority targets. It punishes mid-range, low-mobility armies that cannot prevent Infernus Squads closing to the 12" bracket, where the Strength bonus and volume fire overwhelm multi-wound infantry and light vehicles simultaneously. Armies with reliable deep-strike denial, high-toughness monsters that shrug the damage spike, or fast melee threats that lock the Infernus Squads in combat before they can shoot crack this list open by neutralising its narrow optimal engagement range.
488: Built around Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Tankbustas, Flash Gitz, Big Mek Dakkarigs, and Wazdakka Gutsmek, all ferried forward in Trukks with Gretchin carpeting objectives behind them, this is a Dread Mob list that weaponizes its random shooting table — or cherry-picks the result it needs — to punch far above typical Ork firepower. The plan is to close the mid-board with transported shooters, trigger the Waaagh! to stack More Dakka!'s Sustained Hits 1 onto Infantry units already benefiting from Assault, then unload overlapping anti-tank and anti-infantry volleys that flood out through sheer shot volume. It punishes mid-density elite armies that lack the bodies to absorb Gretchin screen denial while also struggling to survive concentrated Shokk Attack Gun and Loota output. It cracks under alpha-strike pressure that dismantles Trukks before cargo deploys, stranding expensive shooting units in the open with no delivery.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar, Victrix Honour Guard, Repulsor Executioners, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, supported by a flexible infantry core of Scouts, Intercessors, Incursors, and Jump Pack Assault Intercessors, this is a cycling Combat Doctrine gunline that keeps its damage profile relevant across the whole game — Calgar's ability to reselect already-used Doctrines means the buff engine never truly expires. The plan is to park armoured firepower behind cheap infantry screens, rotate Doctrines to match whatever phase or target type matters most, and use mobile elements to contest objectives while the guns do work. It punishes infantry-heavy lists and slow midfield armies that can't threaten the Repulsors at range, stacking sustained fire from multiple heavy platforms simultaneously. It cracks open against elite low-drop armies or aggressive alpha-strike forces that can bypass the screens and pressure the tanks before the Doctrine cycling pays off.
428: Built around Riptides, Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinders, Piranhas, Broadsides, Crisis Starscythes, a Stormsurge, The Twin Lance, and an Ethereal, this is a mobile heavy-firepower list running Mont'Ka, which grants every ranged weapon [ASSAULT] and layers [LETHAL HITS] onto Guided units for the first three battle rounds. The plan is to move aggressively, keep multiple units in the Guided network via Pathfinders, and dump Lethal Hits-boosted firepower into armoured targets while Piranhas and Stealth Suits contest midboard objectives and deny screens. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — the combination of [ASSAULT] mobility, [LETHAL HITS] on guided shots, and redundant heavy platforms creates an anti-tank overload that durable single-piece threats cannot trade into efficiently. It cracks when faced with dense infantry hordes or fast alpha-strike pressure that collapses the Pathfinder guidance network before the kill window opens, leaving Riptides and Broadsides firing without the Lethal Hits multiplier they depend on.
483: Built around Genestealers, Broodlords, Von Ryan's Leapers, Lictors, Neurolictors, Norn Emissaries, Neurotyrant, Zoanthropes, Biovores, and Tyrannofex, this is a highly mobile, multi-threat swarm running primarily the Talons of the Norn Queen detachment, with its Norn Emissaries benefiting from Protean Purpose. The plan is to flood every angle of the board simultaneously — fast melee packages like Genestealers and Leapers threaten objectives mid-table while Lictors and Neurolictors disrupt and deny, and Biovores plus Tyrannofex apply pressure from range to force awkward trade decisions. It punishes armies that can only address one or two threats per turn, as the sheer volume of independent kill vectors overwhelms single-axis defensive schemes. It cracks apart against elite gunlines or high-volume anti-infantry firepower that can strip melee units before they engage, leaving the scoring engine gutted before it lands a punch.
490: Built around Sekhetar Robots buffed by Psyker auras, Defilers, Forgefiends, Tzaangor Shamans, Exalted Sorcerers on Disc, Ahriman, and Daemon Princes with Wings, this is a Psyker-engine war machine list that fuses heavy firepower with melee threat. The Sekhetar Cohort detachment grants Robots' attacks the Psychic keyword and boosts their melee WS through nearby Psyker Infusion auras, while Warpforged Cabal layers hit, wound, and damage re-rolls onto Vehicles like Defilers and Forgefiends when a Psyker stands within 6". The win condition is stacking Psyker proximity bonuses to make multiple Vehicle and Robot activations punishing across both shooting and fighting phases simultaneously. It punishes medium-armour lists that cannot spread thin enough to avoid the overlapping aura bubbles, grinding them down with layered anti-armour volume. Armies that can threaten the fragile Psyker characters at range — collapsing the aura network before it activates — or that can outpace the relatively slow robot-and-vehicle core with aggressive objective pressure will crack this build open.
489: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour buffing Scarab Occult Terminators and Rubric Marines, supported by Daemon Princes of Tzeentch with Wings, Sekhetar Robots, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and Chaos Spawn as ablative screening bodies, the Hexwarp Thrallband floods the table with layered infantry while keeping key units inside the Flow of Magic to unlock its detachment-wide benefits. The plan is to seize and hold at least half the No Man's Land objectives early, extending the Flow of Magic outward so buffed shooting from Enlightened bows and gunline elements can operate at full potency while the Terminator core grinds through midfield brawls. This build punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armies that cannot contest multiple objectives simultaneously, burying them under sheer model count and layered lethality before they can concentrate firepower. It cracks open badly against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can torch the screening chaff on turn one and deny that No Man's Land control before the Flow of Magic ever expands.
427: Built around Crisis Battlesuits in every flavour — Sunforge, Starscythe, Fireknife — alongside Commander Farsight, multiple Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, The Twin Lance, Stealth Battlesuits, and Pathfinders, this is a wall-to-wall battlesuit army running Kauyon as its primary detachment. The plan is to survive early turns screening with Stealth Battlesuits and Vespid Stingwings while Pathfinders light up targets, then detonate in rounds three through five when Kauyon's Sustained Hits 1 and ignore-modifier buff turns the entire army into a precision kill machine. It punishes armour-heavy and multi-wound lists hard, with mobile anti-tank firepower that can reposition and delete key pieces across the mid-table. Armies that can alpha-strike the screening layer or deny Spotting chains before round three starve the engine of its payoff window entirely.
484: Built around Norn Assimilators, Norn Emissaries, Biovores, Pyrovores, Psychophage, and the Swarmlord under Assimilation Swarm, this is a regenerating monster-heavy swarm that keeps its threats alive through Harvester-driven wound recovery and model returns each Command phase. The win condition is grinding attrition: Norns flex their role via Protean Purpose to answer whatever the opponent brings, while Biovores apply indirect pressure and Pyrovores clear infantry screens so the bigger creatures can brawl for primary. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that rely on surgical kills to remove threats, because regeneration means the investment often doesn't stick. Dense board states with fast chaff and high-volume anti-monster shooting crack it open by overwhelming the regeneration math before the Harvesters can cycle.
518: Built around Nekrosor Ammentar, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Skorpekh Lords, Lokhust Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, and Lychguard under the Cursed Legion detachment, this is a wall-to-wall Destroyer Cult army that weaponizes the detachment's Strength-boosting cascade — every destroyed or halved unit triggers a further Strength buff, turning a functional kill chain into a snowballing threat across the board. The plan is to punch through one unit, trigger the cascade, then redirect that elevated Strength into the next target, simultaneously contesting midfield with mobile melee threats while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers crack hard targets at range. It punishes mid-toughness elite armies that cannot screen effectively, because the kill-chain mechanic rewards clustering and Ophydian Destroyers can bypass screens entirely. Lists that apply consistent pressure before the cascade triggers — particularly volume high-AP shooting — can strip units piecemeal and deny the snowball before it starts.
517: Built around the Silent King, paired Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancer support, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers in the Starshatter Arsenal detachment, this is a mobile, layered threat list that contests every zone of the board simultaneously. The core engine is Starshatter's hit bonus on objective-range attacks, letting Doomsday Arks and Vehicles punish anything sitting on a marker while Wraiths, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers deep-strike or flank to deny or flip secondary objectives. It punishes static gunlines hard — massing mobile threats from multiple angles forces impossible target-priority decisions against armies that cannot reposition. Highly mobile elite armies that ignore objectives and fight on their own terms, or lists with enough volume to strip the screen and isolate the Silent King before Technomancer reanimation can keep pace, will crack it open.
530: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Shield-Captains in both Allarus and jetbike configurations, Witchseekers, Blade Champion, Custodian Guard, and Custodian Wardens, this Lions Of The Emperor list weaponizes deliberate spacing — keeping units isolated to trigger the detachment's +1 to hit and +1 to wound on every attack. The win condition is sustained attrition across the whole board: mobile elite units threaten objectives from multiple angles while the hit-and-wound bonus turns already-punishing Custodes profiles into assembly-line killing machines. It punishes mid-durability armies that can't trade efficiently — lists without true hard counters to multi-wound elites get ground down unit by unit before they can stabilize. The fatal crack is massed screening and tight coherency play that forces friendly bubbles, collapsing the isolation bonus and leaving expensive models swinging at full-difficulty rolls.
525: Built around Land Speeder Vengances, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Land Speeders, Sammael, and Lion El'Jonson leading a dense Ravenwing combined-arms force under Company of Hunters and Darkflight Pursuit. The plan is to Advance every turn while firing freely — Company of Hunters grants ASSAULT to all ranged attacks and lets Mounted units shoot after Advancing, while Darkflight Pursuit strips cover from every RAVENWING FLY unit, meaning the skimmer gunline hits full-weight regardless of terrain — and Recon Hunter (carried by nearly two-thirds of lists) supercharges the screen-and-score layer. This build punishes static elite infantry and entrenched gunlines hard, as Ignores Cover demolishes fortified-position defensive setups and mobile anti-armour overloads single-target-removal armies that can't deal with a swarm of fast platforms. It cracks open against armies that can mass-delete light vehicles in one activation, since the individual speeders are fragile and losing the volume of fire quickly collapses the whole damage engine.
529: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators led by Logan Grimnar and Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Ragnar Blackmane, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Priests, and Grey Hunters and Blood Claws flooding the mid-table, all running Saga of the Beastslayer to give every model Lethal Hits against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles once the Beastslayer tally threshold is met. The win condition is completing the Saga early by hunting enemy Characters and big targets with the Terminator brick, then unleashing army-wide Lethal Hits across the horde to grind through secondaries and hold ground with sheer body count. The mass of Grey Hunters and Blood Claws — further split at deployment via Veterans of the Fang — punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear objectives against this volume of ablative wounds. However, high-volume mortal wound output or strong alpha-strike lists that delete the Terminator brick before the Saga completes strip the army of its Lethal Hits payoff and leave a horde without a reliable kill engine.
521: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Ghostkeels, Riptides, Broadsides, and Commander Shadowsun operating under Advanced Acquisition Cadre and Kauyon, this list floods the board with hard-to-shift harassment units that retain hidden status while shooting and then detonate into Sustained Hits 1 across rounds three through five. The win condition is attrition-through-positioning: Pathfinders and Stealth Suits spot and screen while Riptides and Broadsides deliver sustained, modifier-ignoring fire into spotted targets during the back half of the game. It punishes mid-range gunlines and light-armour spam through mobile anti-armour overload — Piranhas and Ghostkeels threaten flanks while the heavy platforms clean up exposed vehicles. However, aggressive early alpha strikes that collapse the screening layer before Kauyon activates leave the fire-support core exposed and unable to leverage its late-game payoff.
441: Built around Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and dual Librarians (one in Terminator armour) with Azrael as the command anchor, this list runs the Librarius Conclave to cycle psychic disciplines each battle round — Divination for re-rolls into elite targets, Biomancy to push Terminator-armoured units deeper faster, Pyromancy when light infantry cluster up. The win condition is delivering mace-swinging Deathwing Knights and Companions into mid-board fights while Temporal Corridor repositions them and Azrael's aura keeps them swinging, backed by Sternguard and Intercessors holding objectives under Unforgiven Task Force's OC-buffed staying power. It punishes slow elite armies that can't clear durable Terminator bodies from scoring zones before the melee wave arrives. It cracks against fast screening armies and anti-tank overload lists that delete the Terminator units in transit before they reach engagement range.
550: Built around multiple Lords of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, Be'lakor, Screamers, and Flamers, this list runs the Lords Of The Warp detachment to stack +1 Leadership and Objective Control on its non-monster Characters, layering in the Scintillating Legion's Flux token re-rolls to squeeze maximum efficiency from every Tzeentch damage roll. The win condition is aggressive board control through fast, multi-threat pressure — Screamers harass and reposition across midfield while Flamers delete infantry screens, freeing Lords of Change and Kairos to dictate scoring lanes with their imposing OC footprints. It punishes infantry-heavy lists brutally, as Flamers' layered mortal output combined with Flux-fuelled re-rolls overwhelms low-save hordes before they can contest. It cracks open against high-volume anti-monster shooting that bypasses its re-roll efficiency and forces saves at scale simultaneously.
551: Built around Skarbrand, Bloodthirsters, Rendmasters on Blood Thrones, Bloodcrushers, Bloodletters, Flesh Hounds, and Bloodmasters surging forward under Blood Legion, with Nurglings and Plaguebearers providing a resilient scoring and screening foundation. The engine is relentless melee pressure: Blood Legion's surge move punishes opponents for moving near Khorne units, letting the army claw back charge range reactively, while Warptide (70% of lists) allows Battleline units to advance and still charge, collapsing the gap every single turn and funnelling enormous layered lethality into close combat. This build punishes infantry-heavy and mid-table brawler armies that must move forward to score — every approach triggers surge opportunities and dumps a flood of high-volume, multi-keyword melee attacks that stack lethal wounds across the board. It cracks open against heavy ranged armies that can sit back, strip screens before the wave lands, and avoid triggering Blood Legion's reactive surges, exploiting the list's minimal shooting and dependence on closing distance unimpeded.
459: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Leman Russ variants, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is a mechanised gunline that layers the Designation Force detachment's Signal Flares ability — granted to Scout Sentinels and Astra Militarum Infantry Smoke units — to mark targets before unleashing a wall of armoured firepower across multiple tank squadrons. The plan is to use Sentinels as forward spotters while Hellhounds flush infantry off objectives and Leman Russ and Rogal Dorn platforms delete armour at range, with Enginseers keeping the metal tide operational. It punishes slow, heavily armoured lists that cannot close distance quickly, stacking anti-tank volume from multiple Squadron units to overwhelm repair economies and overload saves. Aggressive fast melee threats that can reach the gunline early crack it open, since tanks stripped of screening are vulnerable to being tied up in Engagement Range before the shooting phase resolves.
465: Built around Daemonettes, Defilers, Lords Exultant, Infractors, Tormentors, and Chaos Rhinos running the Carnival of Excess detachment, this list pairs Legions of Excess daemons with Emperor's Children infantry in tight mutual-support bubbles to keep everything Empowered — granting Sustained Hits across the board — while Rhinos deliver Infractors and Tormentors directly into the mid-board. The win condition is layered attrition and objective control: flood the centre with horde Daemonettes backed by Defilers' anti-armour threat, punishing opponents who spread thin trying to answer both. It absolutely punishes elite-infantry and light-vehicle lists that can't absorb the volume of Sustained Hits attacks generated by stacked Empowered units fighting in close proximity. Hard counter-pressure from long-range high-AP shooting or tight screen denial collapses the proximity bubbles the list depends on, stranding key units out of their Empowered range.
546: Built around the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, and a supporting screen of Immortals and Flayed Ones, this Hand of the Dynasty list masses C'tan Shards as its primary threat pieces while using Assault-buffed Immortals to perform actions without losing shooting efficiency. The win condition is overwhelming priority-target overload — opponents cannot dedicate enough anti-monster resources to kill multiple C'tan in a single turn, letting survivors walk objectives and grind attrition through reanimation. Hand of the Dynasty's Assault rule lets Immortals advance-and-action freely, keeping scoring pressure constant while the C'tan brawl in the midfield. The build cracks against elite armies that concentrate high-AP, high-volume damage into one turn and delete C'tan faster than they can be replaced, since the entire threat engine collapses when the anchor monsters die early.
544: Built around multiple Skorpekh Lord-led Skorpekh Destroyer units, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Nekrosor Ammentar, Illuminor Szeras, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers under Lokhust Lords, the Silent King, and Ophydian Destroyers, this Awakened Dynasty list weaponizes the detachment's +1 to Hit across nearly every combat and shooting unit on the table. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Ophydians and Skorpekhs hunt infantry midboard while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and the Void Dragon crack vehicles, with Enaegic Dermal Bond keeping lead characters alive long enough to cycle damage into scoring turns. It punishes lists with spread-out, mid-toughness targets that can't absorb simultaneous melee and heavy anti-armour pressure from multiple angles. Concentrated alpha-strike armies or elite high-damage output can strip the attached characters before the hit-bonus engine fires, unraveling the whole threat package.
526: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Lychguard, and the Overlord with Translocation Shroud, this is a multi-vector Necron murder machine that floods the board with fast, durable threat vectors across multiple phases. The plan is to overwhelm opponents by projecting lethal ranged pressure through Lokhust Destroyers and the Void Dragon while Ophydian Destroyers threaten sudden melee eruptions from unexpected angles, forcing opponents to defend multiple kill zones simultaneously rather than concentrating resources. Its high mobility toolkit punishes slower, static gunlines that can't reposition quickly enough to address threats from all directions at once. It cracks open against tight alpha-strike armies and anything capable of stripping the Lokhust Destroyers before they activate, since losing that ranged backbone early collapses the layered threat structure the entire plan depends on.
556: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Mozrog Skragbad, and waves of Boyz and Gretchin, this War Horde list turns every melee weapon in the army into a Sustained Hits 1 engine, drowning opponents in bonus hits across dozens of models. The plan is to crash a layered wall of bodies into the midboard on turns one and two — Trukks delivering Boyz and Boss Snikrot's infiltrating screens cutting off safe positions — then leverage Sustained Hits 1 across multiple large units to grind through any defensive line. It absolutely punishes low-model-count armies with expensive units, where the sheer volume of Sustained Hits attacks overloads both saves and damage-mitigation stacking. Shooting-heavy lists that can strip the horde before contact, or elite melee armies with high enough toughness and armour to absorb the incoming attacks, crack it open before Ghazghkull's momentum gets going.
558: Built around warbikers in multiple large squads, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Deffkoptas, Deffkilla Wartrikes, Gretchin screens, and Trukks, this is a wall of fast, disposable metal that hits you from turn one. The Kult of Speed detachment lets Speed Freeks shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back, meaning the entire bike line threatens every turn regardless of position — the win condition is drowning the midboard in bodies, contesting every objective simultaneously while the faster elements like Deffkoptas punch into priority targets. It punishes low-mobility armies that cannot contest the middle, overwhelming static gunlines before they can focus-fire the swarm down efficiently. 533: Built around multiple Commanders in Coldstar Battlesuits, Crisis Sunforge and Starscythe Battlesuits, Crisis Fireknife Battlesuits, Commander Farsight, Stealth Battlesuits, Broadsides, and Pathfinders with Darkstrider, all running Experimental Prototype Cadre stacked with Kauyon — the +6" range on Battlesuit Characters extends threat envelopes dramatically, while Kauyon's Sustained Hits 1 and modifier-ignoring Guided attacks from rounds three through five turn the mid-to-late game into a slaughter. It cracks under lists that can strip the Pact-empowered vehicles before they activate, or that out-screen the Cultists and deny the mid-board presence the whole engine depends on.
647: Built around Defilers, Chosen, Cultist Mobs, Abaddon, Huron Blackheart, Red Corsairs Raiders, Masters of the Maelstrom, and Chaos Bikers, this Pactbound Zealots list is a melee-forward armoured brawler with serious anti-tank reach — Defilers anchor the firepower while Chosen and Abaddon push into the midfield backed by cheap Cultist screens. The win condition is to grind the centre through sheer threat saturation: Lethal Hits on a 5+ in melee turns every combat into a critical-fish blender, while Huron and Masters of the Maelstrom generate the command resources to keep that pressure sustained across multiple turns. It punishes slow, heavily-armoured gunlines that can't prevent the contact — once Defilers and Bikers pin the flanks, the melee wave hits with Critical Hit volume that few durable targets survive. Armies with strong deep-strike denial or elite chaff-clearing shooting can strip the Cultist screens early, leaving the expensive melee pieces exposed before they close distance.
470: Built around packs of War Dog Karnivores, Brigands, Executioners, and Stalkers screened by Cultist Mobs, the Houndpack Lance floods the board with fast, layered Chaos Knight armor across every phase. The win condition is locking the detachment's Sustained Hits 1 designation onto the opponent's most dangerous unit each Command phase, then concentrating multiple War Dog activations to delete it while lighter cultist chaff holds home objectives. This volume of mobile anti-armor punishes elite vehicle-heavy lists that can't trade efficiently against eight-plus War Dog chassis simultaneously. The build cracks open against armies that can saturate it with screening infantry early, denying the War Dogs clean charges while picking apart the relatively fragile cultist objective holders.
649: Built around Huron Blackheart, Abaddon, Chosen, Cultist Mobs, Masters of the Maelstrom, Red Corsairs Raiders, and Defilers, this is a mass-infantry swarm backed by elite killers and mid-table brawling muscle. The gameplan floods objectives with expendable Cultists and Raiders as cheap bodies while Chosen and Abaddon punch through whatever threatens the scoring pieces, with Masters of the Maelstrom amplifying command economy to sustain the pressure across multiple turns. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear volume, overwhelming their efficient removal with sheer attrition while Defilers provide layered fire that forces difficult priority calls. Armies with high-volume, low-AP shooting or board-wide mortal wound output can strip the horde screen faster than it replaces itself, leaving the expensive combat pieces exposed and stranded.
635: Built around Land Speeder Vengances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Deathwing Knights, Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, and Scout Squads, this is a fast-moving Dark Angels force that leverages the Darkflight Pursuit detachment to give all RAVENWING FLY units Ignores Cover on their ranged attacks, stripping defensive terrain bonuses from enemies across the board. However, elite elite melee threats that can close distance quickly and overload the Deathwing Knights before the speeders reposition will crack this list open, as the flying units are fragile and the infantry core is thin.
652: Built around Abaddon the Despoiler, Kravek Morne, Defilers, Venomcrawlers, and Chaos Bikers, with Cultist Mobs, Nurglings, and Beasts of Nurgle flooding the board beneath them inside Pactbound Zealots — a detachment granting Critical Hits on unmodified 5+ melee rolls to every unit. The plan is to drown opponents in layered melee threat: cheap Nurgle chaff locks down objectives and absorbs return fire while the heavier hitters — Defilers, Bikers, and Venomcrawlers — crash into armour and mid-table brawls with lethal-hit-amplified attacks. It punishes lists that rely on small elite units or light vehicle screens, because the sheer volume of Critical Hits from multiple simultaneous threats overloads defensive resources. It cracks against armies that can shoot the chaff off objectives at range before the melee engine engages, leaving Abaddon and the walkers exposed and unsupported.
638: Built around Ravenwing Black Knights, Ravenwing Command Squads, Outrider Squads, and Azrael supported by Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and Lion El'Jonson, this is a high-mobility biker hammer that floods the midfield with fast, durable threats. The plan is to use speed to dominate primary scoring zones while the Black Knights and Command Squads generate enough combat pressure that opponents are forced to dedicate resources to clearing bikes rather than contesting objectives, with Deathwing Knights and Inner Circle Companions landing as a brutal close-quarters counter-punch. It punishes gunline armies that struggle to clear multiple durable, fast-moving units simultaneously, overwhelming static defenders through sheer board coverage and mobile anti-armour output. It cracks under concentrated alpha-strike pressure or against armies that can efficiently trade into bikes at range, since losing early momentum collapses both the primary-scoring engine and the combat threat simultaneously.
640: Built around Azrael, multiple Inner Circle Companions squads, Deathwing Knights, and a dense Librarian core running the Librarius Conclave alongside the Inner Circle Task Force, this is a psychic-buffed elite infantry army that floods midfield with hard-to-remove bodies. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't clear multiple tough infantry blobs per turn, especially when Celerity and Temporal Corridor keep key units repositioning ahead of the threat. Lists that spam high-volume mortal wound output or saturation shooting can strip the elite infantry faster than the psychic buffs can compensate, and with only middling ranged firepower the army struggles to crack heavily armored targets at range.
451: Built around Archons leading Incubi and Drazhar in Raiders and Venoms, supported by Scourges with heavy weapons, Ravagers, Mandrakes, Kabalite Warriors, Lady Malys, and Cronos, this build spreads across multiple detachments — primarily Kabalite Cartel and Tools of Torment — to layer shooting, melee, and durability pressure simultaneously. It punishes static or low-mobility armies that struggle to answer both the skimmer gunline and the disembarking melee blender at the same time, overwhelming their threat-assessment bandwidth. Armies with reliable high-volume mortal wounds or anti-horde saturation that can strip transports before they deliver crack it open, stranding expensive melee payloads in the open.
596: Built around Librarians (both on foot and in Terminator armour), Deathwatch Veterans, Indomitor Kill Teams, Deathwatch Terminator Squads, and Sternguard Veterans operating under the Bastion Task Force and Librarius Conclave detachments, this is a heavy gunline that floods the board with elite infantry crammed into transports. It punishes static elite armies that can't threaten the transport bubble, overwhelming them with layered small-arms and special weapons before they close distance. Armies that can strip transports early or apply volume mortal-wound pressure crack it open, since the infantry inside loses both its mobility and its action-economy engine simultaneously.
654: Built around Lady Malys, Drazhar, Incubi, Wyches, Reavers, Mandrakes, and wall-to-wall Venoms, this list floods the board with cheap, fast bodies while ferrying its elite killers inside transports under the Skysplinter Assault detachment. It punishes gunline armies and low-model-count lists that cannot absorb the sheer volume of Ignores Cover shooting and Lance-boosted charges hitting from multiple vectors at once. It cracks open when opponents field enough board presence to block disembark lanes, strand transports out of position, or bring anti-horde volume that bleeds the swarm faster than Lady Malys and the Cronos can sustain it.
672: Built around Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Daemon Princes with Wings, Defilers, Noise Marines, and Chaos Rhinos, this is a transport-heavy mechanised assault list running Coterie of the Conceited, where pledging accurate kill counts to Slaanesh each round generates the Pact points that fuel the army's power. The win condition is a coordinated mid-table brawl: Rhinos deliver Infractors and Noise Marines into scoring positions while Lords Exultant buff their output and Defilers and Daemon Princes provide mobile anti-armour that pressures backfield threats. It punishes gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that cannot clear multiple waves of transported infantry arriving on objectives every round. Boards with strong deepstrike denial or high-volume mortal wound output crack it open by destroying units before they activate, making the Slaanesh pledge impossible to fulfill and starving the army of Pact points entirely.
675: Built around Chaos Spawn, Infractors, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Defilers, Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, and Lucius the Eternal, all ferried forward in Rhinos with a winged Daemon Prince providing mobile threat, this is a mid-table brawler that floods objectives with cheap, durable chaff while elite melee infantry do the killing. The core engine is Infractors and Tormentors piling out of transports to contest and fight, with Spawn soaking return fire and Lords Exultant amplifying nearby units into dangerous combat threats. It punishes infantry-heavy armies that can't clear durable chaff efficiently, letting Spawn screen key pieces while Flawless Blades and Noise Marines grind through lighter targets. Armies that pack high-volume anti-armour or elite melee that ignores its screening layer can crack the transport bubble early and strand key units before they reach engagement range.
633: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Hyperadapted Raveners, Patriarch, Benefictus, Deathleaper, Neophyte Hybrids, Acolyte Hybrids, Reductus Saboteur, and Achilles Ridgerunners operating under the Final Day detachment — which allows a substantial Tyranid Vanguard Invader contingent to supplement the cult's native swarm. The plan is to drown opponents in layered waves: Neophyte Hybrids with Xenocult Masses healing 3 wounds per Command phase anchor objectives while Genestealers and Raveners punch into mid-board brawls, with Deathleaper and the Reductus Saboteur disrupting backlines ahead of the main assault. It punishes armies that rely on thin screening lines or low model counts, simply overwhelming threat saturation with more dangerous bodies than opponents can prioritize in a single turn. Armies with high volumes of mortal-wound output or elite alpha-strike potential crack this build by removing key pieces before the layered assault can compound.
688: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, and Interceptor Squads screened by Strike Squads, this is a mobile hammer list that floods the board with heavy walkers and teleporting infantry across a detachment-agnostic framework of Immaterial Interdiction and Sanctic Spearhead. It punishes slower armoured lists that cannot contest mid-board efficiently, as multiple high-damage walkers advancing at threat ranges most opponents aren't built to handle across the whole table. However, mass high-volume shooting or deep-strike denial armies that can isolate and focus individual Dreadknights before they consolidate will crack the list open, since losing even one walker early collapses the damage math significantly.
634: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Achilles Ridgerunners, Acolyte Hybrids with hand flamers, Neophyte Hybrids, Atalan Jackals, Reductus Saboteurs, and a Patriarch supported by Benefictus psykers, this is a mass-horde gunline that hits in multiple layers across the table. Ridgerunners and hand-flamer Acolytes punish clustered infantry hordes hard, while the layered threat of melee, flame, and mobile anti-armour overloads lists that can only answer one axis at a time. Elite, low-model-count armies that deny terrain, limit objective spread, or alpha-strike the Neophyte anchor before healing triggers will crack this list open quickly.
689: Built around Grand Master Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Strike Squads, Castellan Crowe with Purifiers, and Brotherhood Terminators, this Brotherhood Strike list uses deep strike as its primary delivery mechanism — every unit that drops in re-rolls hit and wound rolls of 1, turning arrival turns into focused kill windows. It punishes static, elite lists that can't reposition away from multi-angle drops, especially when Tome of Forbidden Ways amplifies the psychic-strike threat on arrival turns. What cracks it is aggressive screen-and-deny — early board control that collapses safe deep strike lanes forces pieces into poor positions and neuters the synchronized arrival timing the whole plan depends on.
615: Built around Berehk Stornbröw, Einhyr Hearthguard, Cthonian Beserks, Kâhl, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, this list blends a brutally tough mid-board brawling core with a punishing heavy gunline, ferried forward by Sagitaurs and Kapricus Carriers. However, fast alpha-strike armies that can screen the mid-board and prevent the 9" engagement bubble from forming will neutralize the core wound re-roll engine before it ever fires.
700: Built around Cerastus Knight Lancers and the Knight Castellan, this is a highly mobile big-Knight list running the Questoris Companions detachment, which rewards aggressive Oath cycling by unlocking additional Oaths each turn as you complete them. The engine is momentum-based: keep fulfilling Oaths to stack bonuses, use the Lancers' speed to threaten priority targets early, and let the Castellan's long-range firepower punish anything that tries to stay back. The mobile anti-armour toolkit brutally overloads opposing armies that rely on massed vehicles or monsters, cycling Oaths to maintain pressure across every phase. Lists that can screen charge lanes, deny the Lancers space to engage, or strip Hull Points through volume anti-tank fire before Oaths generate meaningful tempo will crack this build open fastest.
621: Built around Hekaton Land Fortresses, Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, Sagitaurs, Einhyr Hearthguard, and a dense supporting cast of Hearthkyn Warriors, Yaegirs, Arkanyst Evaluators, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, this is a mid-board brawling gunline that floods the table with durable vehicles and cheap screening bodies across several detachment flavors. The plan is to park Hekatons as mobile firebase hubs, using their Transport auras to buff embarked or nearby infantry, while Pioneers and Sagitaurs contest midfield objectives and the Hearthguard punch into whatever needs to die up close. It punishes slower, static gunlines that can't clear volume efficiently — the sheer number of units and vehicles demands more firepower than most elite lists can muster in a single turn. However, concentrated high-AP anti-tank fire cracks the Hekatons early and collapses the firebase scaffolding, leaving the support infantry exposed and underperforming without their combat bubbles.
617: Built around Hernkyn Yaegirs, Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, this is a mid-board gunline that floods the table with fast-moving infantry and heavy firepower platforms. The Farseekers detachment's +1 to hit within 12" rewards aggressive positioning — the plan is to push Hernkyn units into mid-range, lock down objectives with transported hearthkyn and Einhyr Hearthguard, and grind out YP through kills to fuel secondary scoring. It punishes slow, durable armies that expect to survive attrition, as massed Thunderkyn and Land Fortress fire can overwhelm high-toughness targets that rely on wound thresholds rather than volume saves. Highly mobile, screen-heavy forces or alpha-strike lists that can collapse the mid-board before the +1 hit bonus activates will expose how fragile the scoring engine becomes when the Hernkyn units are pushed off their optimal range bracket.
620: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Kapricus Carriers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, and a dense supporting cast of infantry and transports, this Farseekers list blends a mechanised mid-table brawler with a punishing gunline. The Farseekers detachment's +1 to hit within 12" on Hernkyn units pulls the whole army forward aggressively, while Thunderkyn and Steeljacks pour concentrated fire into whatever the Pioneers pin down, generating YP through kills to fuel secondary detachment payoffs. It thrives against mid-density armies that can't screen the advance, as the combination of massed short-range firepower, transport protection, and layered lethality overwhelms anything that lets the Kin get close. Spread-thin, high-unit-count hordes or fast alpha-strike lists that deny the 12" sweet spot and strip the Kapricus Carriers early can fracture the engine before it gets rolling.
619: Built around Ûthar the Destined, Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, this is a heavily armoured mid-table brawler that floods the board with durable infantry, transports, and hard-hitting fire support. The engine is the Hearthguard Covenant's wound re-roll aura at close range — pack Ûthar and Hearthguard into Hekatons, drive into the midfield, and punish anything within 9" with relentless, efficient firepower while Thunderkyn and Sagitaurs provide layered gunline support. It thrives against elite, low-model-count armies where every re-rolled wound at close range compounds, and the sheer volume of durable units makes it brutally hard to trade efficiently against. Spread-thin screening forces and long-range anti-tank that can strip Hekatons before they close the gap are its primary vulnerabilities, as the whole wound re-roll package collapses if the delivery vehicles die early.
616: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Cthonian Berserks, and Kâhl characters riding Hekaton Land Fortresses and Kapricus Carriers forward, this is a Hearthband list that smashes into the midboard and grinds. The engine is forcing every unit to target the closest eligible enemy, unlocking wound-roll rerolls across the board while Hearthguard and Kâhl units gain an extra point of AP on every swing — the plan is to crack open armour through sheer weight of improved AP attacks while Berserks and Thunderkyn clear whatever survives into Engagement Range. It brutally punishes elite, low-model-count armies that cannot absorb repeated high-AP melee and heavy weapon fire simultaneously from multiple angles. Horde lists or anything that screens the midboard aggressively can force unfavourable target priority, denying the closest-target trigger and diluting the AP bonus where it hurts most.
618: Built around Cthonian Beserks, Sagitaurs, Hearthkyn Warriors, Kapricus Carriers, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and the Hekaton Land Fortress, this is a mechanised mid-board brawler that uses Sagitaur's Scouts 6" to crash the midfield on turn one with infantry-packed transports before the opponent can establish a defensive line. The engine is attrition-through-presence: Beserks disembark to contest and grind close-quarters objectives while Thunderkyn and the Land Fortress apply heavy fire support, and the Mercenary Oathband's Hostile Acquisition mechanic rewards sustained board control by generating Ymyr Points to shift objective priority mid-game. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't handle simultaneous threats across multiple objective vectors, as the Scouts move guarantees early pressure before those armies can pre-position screens. Armies with strong alpha-strike deep strike packages or high-volume anti-infantry that can strip transports before the Beserks deploy will crack it open, since the entire kill chain collapses if the mechanised wave is neutralised in transit.
455: Built around Technomancers, Canoptek Wraiths, Flayed Ones, Skorpekh Lords, Skorpekh Destroyers, the Nightbringer, the Void Dragon, and Nekrosor Ammentar, this is a swarming close-combat toolbox that floods the board with independently threatening melee packages across multiple unit types. The plan is to overwhelm opponents across multiple angles simultaneously — C'tan anchor objectives and absorb punishment while Skorpekh and Flayed One kill chains crash into whatever is weakest, with Technomancers keeping key pieces alive through reanimation. It punishes lists that can't project damage across the whole board, as spreading fire thin enough to drop multiple durable, self-healing threats is genuinely difficult. Concentrated high-AP shooting or melee that can delete units in a single activation before reanimation triggers will crack it open, since the engine collapses when pieces die faster than Technomancers can restore them.
659:
Built around the Void Dragon, Nightbringer, Deceiver, one or more Transcendent C'tan, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list fields an overwhelming mass of individually powerful god-monsters and deep-striking melee threats with no single anchor that defines its identity across all lists.

The win condition is elite-unit removal and objective denial by simultaneous pressure — multiple C'tan hit different table quadrants while Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers deep strike directly onto contested objectives, forcing opponents to split answers they rarely have in sufficient volume.

It punishes lists that rely on a single elite damage dealer or centralized screen, since the sheer number of independent C'tan threats guarantees at least two or three engagements the opponent simply cannot adequately answer in the same turn.

Its critical vulnerability is high-volume, point-efficient anti-tank firepower spread across the army: losing one C'tan is survivable, but concentrated shooting that degrades two or three simultaneously collapses the pressure engine before the melee threats can close distance.
658: Built around the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, C'tan Shard of the Deceiver, Ophydian Destroyers, and Imotekh the Stormlord under Pantheon of Woe, this is a monster-mash pressure list that floods the board with Necrons Monster keyword units projecting their Distortion Fields aura — stripping enemy armour saves across the entire battlefield by improving AP on every incoming attack within 6". The win condition is multi-angle threat saturation: park C'tan in your opponent's face to force AP degradation on their own units while Ophydian Destroyers tunnel into flanks, Imotekh provides command support, and the monsters grind through anything they touch. It punishes mid-toughness elite armies and defensive castle lists that rely on strong saves, since Distortion Fields systematically dismantles armour stacking before a shot is even resolved. It struggles against long-range alpha-strike lists that can delete C'tan before the aura does work, and highly mobile armies that avoid the 6" bubble entirely.
603: Built around Tankbustas, Flash Gitz, Lootas, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, and Gretchin blobs backed by Ghazghkull Thraka, Wazdakka Gutsmek, and Zodgrod Wortsnagga, this is a mass-horde gunline that layers specialist shooting behind a wall of cheap bodies. The plan is to activate the Waaagh! and leverage Sustained Hits 1 across the entire infantry line — Tankbustas punishing armour, Flash Gitz and Lootas grinding infantry — while Gretchin screen objectives and Trukks deliver pressure units into mid-table. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that can't clear the screen fast enough to shut down the shooting core before the Waaagh! window opens. Armies that can alpha-strike the Tankbusta squads or outrange the gunline entirely before the Waaagh! activates will crack it open, since the damage engine collapses without those anti-tank bricks intact.
702: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Flash Gitz, Boyz, Nobz, and Breaka Boyz trucking forward in Battlewagons and Trukks, with Gretchin and Kommandos handling the flanks, this is the Freebooter Krew detachment — a mid-board brawling horde that also punches with real shooting weight. The win condition is designating a loot objective each Command phase and flooding it with bodies, then leveraging Sustained Hits 1 on every Orks Infantry, Mounted, and Walker attack to delete whatever contest threatens it. Bannernobs and Git-Spotter Squig keep the kill output consistent while the sheer mass of cheap Gretchin and mobile Boyz makes it brutally efficient at denying opponents primary points through body-volume alone. Armies that can screen effectively and force Ghazghkull's freight train to fight uphill into elite melee or high-AP shooting will crack it open, since the horde's durability depends on volume rather than resilience.
677: Built around multiple Librarians buffing Intercessors, Scout Squads, and Bladeguard Veterans, this list floods mid-table with durable infantry bodies screened by cheap scouts while psyker-fuelled disciplines rotate between movement, accuracy, and firepower depending on the matchup. The win condition is objective saturation through volume — layered infantry screens hold secondaries while Bladeguard punch forward to lock enemy scoring units in melee and Librarian buffs convert mid-strength firepower into meaningful damage trades. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear numerous tough infantry blobs, particularly when Divination Discipline turns mass bolt fire into a reliable grind. However, it cracks under high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that make the infantry density a liability rather than a strength.
678: Built around Marneus Calgar, Captain Titus, Victrix Honour Guard, Wardens of Ultramar, Bladeguard Veterans, Sternguard Veterans, and a Librarian, this Librarius Conclave and Reclamation Force list plays as a layered gunline with elite melee teeth. The core engine is the Reclamation Force's objective-linked AP bonus — stacking Sternguard shooting with Bladeguard and Wardens charging into contested markers to strip AP across both phases while Marneus generates additional attacks — then cycling Divination or Biomancy each round to keep pressure wherever the line needs it. It punishes medium-armour infantry lists brutally, as the AP improvement on objective-range melee attacks turns already-efficient elite units into a meat grinder for anything Save 3+ or worse. Armies that can stay off objectives at range or flood the board with cheap bodies to block the melee commitment — particularly mass-screen builds — can slow the scoring engine and dilute the AP bonus before the elite units get into range.
686:
Built around Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, Intercessors, Scout Squads, and Bladeguard Veterans, this list uses the Fulguris Task Force detachment's ingress rule to surge its entire Speeder battlegroup forward in the first Movement phase, threatening priority targets before the opponent can react.

The engine is mobile anti-armour pressure: Hammerstrikes unload heavy firepower from unexpected angles on turn one while Scouts and Intercessors hold home objectives, and Bladeguard Veterans threaten mid-board control to force the opponent into reactive positioning.

It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armour lists that cannot reposition away from the first-turn Speeder ingress, concentrating lethal anti-tank volume into an early kill window that slower armies cannot answer.

Its fragility is the mirror of its aggression — Speeders are lightly armoured, and any list with strong alpha-strike capability, deep-strike denial, or fast screening units can neutralise the ingress threat before it pays off, leaving the remaining infantry core badly outgunned.
681: Built around multiple Librarians in Terminator Armour, standard Librarians, Terminator Assault Squads, Bladeguard Veterans, and Marneus Calgar cycling the Psychic Disciplines ability each battle round — selecting Biomancy for extra movement, Divination for hit/wound rerolls, or Pyromancy for ranged punishment depending on the game state. The engine is Reclamation Force's objective-anchored AP improvement stacking with Bladeguard and Assault Terminators in melee, while psyker-buffed shooting and Calgar's command weight keep pressure everywhere simultaneously. This build punishes mid-tier armoured lists that cannot handle both a durable objective-holding melee core and a flexible gunline simultaneously, as the round-by-round Discipline switching denies opponents a stable threat assessment. Highly mobile elite armies that out-activate the Terminator blocks before buffs land, or lists with volume high-AP shooting that strips the melee core before it reaches contested objectives, expose the build's dependence on Discipline timing.
679: Built around Marneus Calgar, Cato Sicarius, Victrix Honour Guard, Repulsor Executioners, and Scout and Incursor screens, this list plants itself in terrain and grinds through the Ceramite Sentinels detachment's re-roll-ones-to-hit-and-wound while Entrenched units become substantially harder to dislodge. The engine is a static heavy gunline: Repulsor Executioners deliver sustained anti-armour output from cover while Calgar and Sicarius buff adjacent units, and screens deny opponents the clean charges needed to flush the tanks out. It punishes aggressive mechanised lists that need to push into mid-board, as the combination of Entrenched durability and volume fire overloads anything that has to close the gap. Lists that can apply strong shooting at range, force the Executioners to reposition and lose Entrenched status, or that field enough high-AP anti-infantry to strip screens and expose the supporting characters will crack it open.
695: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators (typically two squads), Logan Grimnar, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Ragnar Blackmane, Blood Claws, and a Wolf Guard Battle Leader, this is a dense, character-stacked melee army running Saga of the Great Wolf and cycling its Hunting Pack selections each Command phase to shift between mobility and accuracy buffs. The plan is to flood mid-table with durable, elite infantry, leverage Grimnar and accompanying characters to amplify Terminator and Headtaker threat, and grind opponents off objectives through sustained close-combat pressure. It punishes slow, static gunlines that lack the volume or positioning to handle multiple concurrent elite threats converging from different angles. It cracks open against armies that can screen aggressively and deny charge lanes, or that output enough AP-heavy firepower to strip Terminators before the melee engine engages.
680: Built around Caanok Var, multiple Terminator Assault Squads, Librarians, Sternguard Veterans, and screening infantry in the Hammer of Avernii detachment, this list plays as a grinding heavy gunline that can redirect its Oath of Moment target mid-battle whenever Caanok Var is alive, ensuring the wound-reroll engine stays active across multiple targets. This punishes elite-heavy armies that present a small number of high-value units, since the Oath chain can track them down one by one and the dense firepower overloads their durability. However, armies that flood the board with cheap, disposable chaff force the Oath engine to burn on low-value targets, and fast close-range threats that bypass the gunline's preferred engagement distance can crack open the relatively slow Terminator core before it repositions.
676: Built around Infernus Squads, Bladeguard Veterans, Librarians, Adrax Agatone, Vulkan He'stan, Scout Squads, Land Raider Redeemers, and Sternguard Veterans, this list combines heavy flame and bolter firepower delivered inside armoured transports with a durable close-range infantry core. 682: Built around Darnath Lysander, Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, Vanguard Veterans with jump packs, Bladeguard Veterans, and a Librarian, this is a dense, multi-wave melee and fire-support list running the Emperor's Shield detachment, which hands Lysander full wound re-rolls against the Oath of Moment target and gives the broader army wound-1 re-rolls on the same target. It struggles against fast, spread-out armies that deny clean Oath of Moment focus and can kite the slow Terminator core, bleeding it for points across multiple objectives before it can consolidate.
528: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Arjac Rockfist, and massed Grey Hunters operating under the Saga Of The Great Wolf detachment, this list floods the table with elite infantry and durable anchor pieces. It punishes lighter infantry armies that can't survive repeated waves of elite melee threats across a wide frontage. However, a focused anti-tank overload or heavy indirect fire can strip its heavier support pieces early, leaving the infantry blobs without the punch needed to crack durable targets.
614: Built around multiple Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, Commander Farsight, the Twin Lance, and a dense core of Crisis Starscythe, Sunforge, and Fireknife suits, this is a battlesuit-wall list that punches hardest inside 12"—where the Retaliation Cadre detachment boosts Strength, and inside 8" adds AP on top. 599: Built around Neurolictor, Lictor, Broodlord-led Genestealer packs, Von Ryan's Leapers, Hyperadapted Raveners, Raveners, and Biovores, with Deathleaper as Warlord via Vanguard Onslaught, this is a deep-striking, multi-wave harassment army that floods the table with fast, independently threatening units. 515: Built around Biovores, Maleceptors, Exocrines, Tyrannofexes, Genestealers, Broodlords, Hormagaunts, Lictors, Norn Emissaries, Neurotyrants, and Neurolictors under Invasion Fleet, this is a mobile Swiss-army-knife swarm that layers ranged firepower over a fast melee threat package. Tight alpha-strike lists that can kill the synapse web early, or elite armies that can simply absorb the shooting and trade efficiently in melee, crack this build open before its layered threat matrix can fully develop.
612: Built around Exalted Eightbound, Eightbound, Slaughterbound, a Daemon Prince of Khorne, and Jakhals screening, this Possessed Slaughterband list is a wall of possessed bodies surging up the board under the Brazen Fury ability — every time an enemy shoots a unit down, the survivors lunge forward an additional D6", turning incoming fire into free advances. It cracks open against elite close-combat armies that can match it blow-for-blow in melee without feeding the surge mechanic, and against deep-strike denial setups that wall off the mid-board before the wave arrives.
708: Built around Allarus Custodians, Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Vertus Praetors, a Blade Champion, a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, and bodies screens of Witchseekers and Prosecutors, this is a mobile combined-arms Custodes force that layers elite melee threats across multiple unit types rather than committing to a single delivery engine. 723: Built around Sydonian Dragoons with taser lances, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Sicarian Infiltrators, Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Skitarii Rangers, and Skorpius Disintegrators, this list layers mobile anti-armour and transported infantry into a cohesive mid-table brawler. 492: Built around Allarus Custodians, Custodian Guard, Blade Champion, Vertus Praetors, Custodian Wardens, Witchseekers, and a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, this list runs Shield Host as its backbone with the Tharanatoi Hammerblow secondary detachment powering Terminator ingress-into-charge sequences. 439: Built around Hastarii Fusiliers, Skitarii Rangers, Vanguard, and Sicarian Infiltrators riding Skorpius Duneriders, led by Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, and a swarm of Tech-Priest Manipuli and Skitarii Marshals, this is a transport-infantry horde that floods the midtable. 741: Built around Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Tempestus Scions, Kasrkin, Gaunt's Ghosts, Scout Sentinels, Krieg Combat Engineers, and a wall of Cadian infantry led by Ursula Creed, this list floods the board with layered, high-volume infantry across multiple detachments — most commonly Designation Force or Combined Arms. It cracks open against high-mobility lists that can outmaneuver the slow advance, bypass the blob entirely, and contest backfield objectives before the grinding attrition engine gets traction.
586: Built around waves of Daemonettes, Fiends, Beasts of Nurgle, Keepers of Secrets, the Contorted Epitome, the Tormentbringer, and the Masque of Slaanesh, this list weaponises both Legion Of Excess and Warptide to create a perpetual-motion assault engine: Daemonettes advance and still charge, Fell Back units re-engage the same turn, and nothing ever truly disengages. 747: Built around War Dog Stalkers, Karnivores, and Brigands — six to eight fast, aggressive light Knights swarming the board with overlapping threat vectors. 750: Built around Cultist Mobs flooding objectives and the Knight Abominant anchoring the battleline, this Iconoclast Fiefdom list imports DAMNED units — primarily Cultists and occasionally Nurglings or Traitor Guardsmen — to swarm low-value board space while big Knights do the killing. 729: Built around Chaos Bikers, Cultist Mobs, Traitor Guardsmen, Defilers, and Chaos Rhinos operating under Pactbound Zealots, this list floods the board with cheap bodies while parking Daemon Engine firepower at range. 725: Built around Ravenwing Command Squads, Outrider Squads, Ravenwing Black Knights, Sammael, Land Speeder Vengences, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Scout Squads, and Azrael, this is a Company of Hunters bike-and-speeder force that operates as a high-speed mobile gunline — every unit fires on the advance or after falling back, denying the opponent the usual trade-off of movement versus firepower. Armies that can delete Speeders early with massed high-volume shooting strip the ranged engine away and leave the elite melee core overexposed and outnumbered on objectives.
642: Built around Deathwing Knights (typically two squads), Chaplains in Terminator armour, Lion El'Jonson, Azrael, Inner Circle Companions, and an Ancient in Terminator armour, this list runs dense elite melee packed into a Terminator shell and splits its detachment across Wrath Of The Rock and Interrogation Conclave depending on list preference. 726: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and Sammael leading Ravenwing Black Knights and a Command Squad, this is a Wrath of the Rock list that floods the board with elite Terminator infantry and fast Mounted units protected by a universal -1 to wound whenever the attacker's Strength exceeds the target's Toughness. It punishes lists that rely on high-Strength, low-volume shooting to crack durable targets, since the wound penalty blunts most anti-tank and anti-elite profiles across both the infantry and Mounted halves of the army simultaneously. It cracks open against mass low-Strength high-volume fire that bypasses the detachment ability entirely, and against armies that can simply outrun or outmaneuver the relatively slow Terminator blocks before the Ravenwing can compensate.
636: Built around multiple Land Speeder Vengeances, regular Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Librarians, Inner Circle Companions, Sternguard Veterans, and Azrael operating under the Librarius Conclave detachment, this list floods the board with fast-moving firepower buffed each battle round by a chosen Psychic Discipline — rotating between re-rolls, movement boosts, or enhanced shooting depending on the matchup. Fusillade on Librarians amplifies the already-dense shooting volume, punishing static gunlines and high-toughness vehicle lists that cannot reposition to avoid the fire. The build cracks under pressure from fast melee armies that can close range before the skimmer screen is established, since the infantry core is durable but not built to absorb a determined alpha strike.
629: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Poxwalkers, Blightlord Terminators, Typhus, Plague Marines, a Tallyman, and a Lord of Virulence, this list runs the Death Lord's Chosen detachment with near-universal Paragons of Putrescence support to push Contagion Range out to 12" on Death Guard Characters, creating overlapping affliction bubbles that bleed mortal wounds off the detachment's end-of-Command-phase roll against every Afflicted enemy unit on a 6 or less. 628: Built around Poxwalkers, Deathshroud Terminators, Lord of Contagion, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Malignant Plaguecasters, Plague Marines, and Typhus, this Paragons of Putrescence list maximises Contagion Range across every Character on the board, pushing debuff auras to 12" to blanket mid-table objectives in overlapping Lethal Hits coverage before a fight is even struck. It punishes melee-reliant armies and light infantry hordes that have to fight through stacked Lethal Hits in the mid-table brawl, where every charge into the pocket costs disproportionate casualties. Heavy shooting armies that can strip Characters at range before the aura network locks in, or fast objective threats that bypass the contagion bubble entirely, expose how static and attrition-dependent the scoring engine truly is.
701: Built around Deathwatch Veterans, Deathwatch Terminators, dual Librarians, and Intercessor squads, this is a mid-table shooting and brawling force that leans on Firestorm Assault Force in most lists to give its ranged weapons Assault and a Strength bump inside 12", turning aggressive repositioning into raw killing power. It struggles against fast elite armies that can bypass the screen, isolate Terminators before they close, and avoid that 12" killzone entirely.
744: Built around Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, Maulerfiends, Defilers, Lords Exultant, Infractors in Rhinos, Tormentors, Noise Marines, and Flawless Blades, this Coterie of the Conceited list drives a wall of mobile threat into the mid-board every turn. 746: Built around Infractors, Chaos Spawn, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, Defilers, and Daemon Princes, delivered primarily via Chaos Rhinos, this is a high-volume melee swarm that floods the midboard with transported infantry and expendable chaff. Coordinated alpha strikes that pop Rhinos before the infantry deploy, or elite melee armies that out-fight Infractors in the brawl, will strip the scoring engine before the Pact point economy gets going.
